text:
Maria: Hi team - customer asking us to fill CAIQ item about key ownership + backup responsibilities. They want a single-sentence answer per control. Can someone confirm who owns keys, disk backups, and logs for Redwood Private vs Hosted?
Alex: I can draft. Quick Q: are we treating Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) as customer-managed keys by default?
Jamie: Correct for Private: customer-managed KMS/HSM is the default. For Hosted API we offer managed keys; customers can request bring-your-own-key (BYOK) in Dedicated/Private via KMS integrations.
Maria: Nice. Customer specifically asked: "Who is responsible for backup lifecycle (retention & deletion) for model artifacts and customer data stored on our platform?"
Alex: Short answer: Redwood handles backups for Hosted/Dedicated (we run snapshot/backup processes and provide deletion APIs and SLA-backed retention). For Private (VPC/on-prem) the customer is responsible unless we have an explicit managed-services add-on.
Jamie: Adding detail for CAIQ: backups for Hosted are encrypted at rest using managed keys by default. If the customer requests BYOK, snapshot encryption uses the customer's KMS. Deletion: we provide admin APIs to trigger data deletion + retention config; final deletion timelines vary by deployment and compliance package.
Maria: Can we put that into a 1-line per item format the security reviewer likes?
Alex: Draft below — feel free to edit.
Alex: ```
Key ownership: Hosted - Redwood-managed keys by default; BYOK via customer KMS available for Dedicated/Private.
Backups: Hosted/Dedicated - Redwood-managed encrypted snapshots with configurable retention; Private - customer-managed unless under a managed-services contract.
Logs/Monitoring data: Redwood retains platform logs for service health (default retention 30d); customer application logs in Private are customer-controlled.
Customer data deletion: We expose deletion APIs and support retention configs; final deletion timing depends on deployment and agreed SLA.```
Taylor: LGTM. Legal nit: for Hosted we should add "subject to contractual terms" after BYOK line.
Alex: Updated.
Alex: ```
Key ownership: Hosted - Redwood-managed keys by default; BYOK via customer KMS available for Dedicated/Private (BYOK subject to contractual terms).
Backups: Hosted/Dedicated - Redwood-managed encrypted snapshots with configurable retention; Private - customer-managed unless under a managed-services contract.
Logs/Monitoring data: Redwood retains platform logs for service health (default retention 30d); customer application logs in Private are customer-controlled.
Customer data deletion: We expose deletion APIs and support retention configs; final deletion timing depends on deployment and agreed SLA.```
Maria: Great. Two follow-ups from the reviewer: 1) they asked if we can map CAIQ control IDs to the above statements, 2) they requested a one-row shared responsibility table.
Jamie: For mapping we'll provide a short mapping doc (CCM/CAIQ ids vary by version). For the table, here's a concise ASCII table we can paste into the CAIQ Excel cell: 
Jamie: ```
Component | Hosted (Redwood) | Dedicated (Redwood) | Private (Customer)
--------- | ---------------- | ------------------- | -------------------
Key Mgmt  | Redwood (managed) / BYOK opt-in | Customer BYOK or Redwood-managed | Customer-managed
Backups   | Redwood-managed snapshots | Redwood-managed or customer option | Customer-managed
Logs      | Platform logs retained by Redwood; app logs customer-controlled | same as Hosted | Customer-controlled
Deletion  | API + retention config (Redwood executes) | API + config | Customer executes unless managed svc
```
Maria: Perfect. Can we also include the exact retention number for platform logs? They asked for a number in the CAIQ response.
Jamie: Default is 30 days for platform operational logs; we can offer 90/365 as an enterprise add-on. I'll include that parenthetically.
Maria: OK last ask: reviewer wants confirmation that encrypted snapshots use customer's keys when BYOK enabled. Jamie you already said that but they want it explicit.
Jamie: Confirmed: when BYOK is enabled we encrypt snapshots with customer-managed KMS keys; we do not retain plaintext keys.
DeployBot: Notice: CAIQ draft updated in https://redwood.internal/docs/caiq-drafts/1776004321-draft (editable) :white_check_mark:
Taylor: Thanks — I'll paste the one-line answers + table into the CAIQ spreadsheet and flag legal for final wording. Maria — want me to cc the reviewer?
Maria: Yes please cc and mention the contractual caveat. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
